_strings.@@df099215ffda: Treaty conformity — KS conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from KS income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the KS return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Kansas Form K-40 starts from federal adjusted gross income (K-40 Line 1: "Federal adjusted gross income (as reported on your federal income tax return)"), and Kansas modifications are made only on Schedule S Part A. The Schedule S Part A "Additions to Federal Adjusted Gross Income" are an enumerated, closed list (lines A1-A7): A1 state/municipal bond interest, A2 KPERS contributions, A3 Kansas expensing recapture, A4 low-income student scholarship contributions, A5 IRC 163(j) business interest expense carryforward, A6 unqualified First-Time Home Buyer savings account withdrawals, and A7 "other additions" (whose instructions list only federal income tax refunds and partnership/S-corp/fiduciary adjustments). There is NO add-back for federally tax-treaty-exempt income anywhere in Part A. Because income exempt under a U.S. tax treaty is already excluded from federal AGI and Kansas has no add-back, it flows through and is not re-taxed by Kansas -> conforms. (Source: 2023 Individual Income Tax Booklet, ip23.pdf, K-40 Line 1 and Schedule S Part A / line-by-line instructions.)

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: 2023 Form K-40, Line 8: "Tax (from Tax Tables or Tax Computation Worksheet)". Instructions (booklet p. 7): "LINE 8 (Tax): If line 7 is $100,000 or less, use the Tax Tables beginning on page 25 to find the amount of your tax. If line 7 is more than $100,000, you will need to use the Tax Computation Worksheet on page 32 to compute your tax." Line 7 = Line 3 (KAGI) minus Line 6 (Line 4 standard/itemized deduction + Line 5 exemption allowance); "if less than zero, enter 0". This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply K-40 Line 3, Kansas adjusted gross income (KAGI) = Line 1 federal AGI ("Federal adjusted gross income (as reported on your federal income tax return)") plus or minus Line 2 net modifications from Schedule S Part A (line A25). Most filers have no Kansas modifications, in which case Line 3 equals federal AGI. The op then subtracts the shipped standard deduction (K-40 Line 4) and the $2,250-per-exemption allowance (Line 5) to reach Line 7 taxable income, to which the rate schedule applies. Tax-table mandate below $100,000: K-40 Line 8 REQUIRES the Tax Tables (booklet pp. 25-31) when Line 7 taxable income is $100,000 or less; the Tax Computation Worksheet (p. 32) is used only above $100,000. The table uses $50-wide bands, so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within a table band — the filed form must use the table. Zero-liability floor is a CLIFF, not a marginal zero bracket: the 2023 Kansas Tax Table prints $0 tax for taxable income of $2,500 or less (Single/HOH/MFS) and $5,000 or less (Married Filing Joint), and just above the threshold tax is 3.1% of the ENTIRE taxable income (table: $2,501-$2,550 -> $78; MFJ $5,001-$5,050 -> $156). The Tax Computation Worksheet's income ranges likewise begin at $2,501/$5,001. This op's marginal bracket math cannot represent the cliff: for taxable income at or below $2,500/$5,000 the true Kansas tax is $0, and this op will overstate it by up to about $78 (Single/HOH/MFS) or $155 (MFJ). Rounded worksheet constants (Single/HOH/MFS only): the 2023 Tax Computation Worksheet subtraction amounts $323 (5.25% row) and $458 (5.7% row) are the exact cumulative-bracket values $322.50 and $457.50 rounded up by $0.50, so for taxable income over $100,000 the filed worksheet result can be $1 LOWER than pure marginal bracket math after rounding. The MFJ constants ($645 and $915) equal the exact cumulative sums, so MFJ worksheet results match marginal math exactly. One rate schedule covers Single, Head of Household, and Married Filing Separate (the booklet prints a single combined column/schedule for all three); it is duplicated per status here. Married Filing Joint has its own schedule with bracket breaks at exactly twice the other statuses' ($30,000/$60,000 vs $15,000/$30,000). Qualifying surviving spouse maps to HEAD OF HOUSEHOLD in Kansas, not MFJ: the 2023 booklet Filing Status instruction says 'If your federal filing status is Qualifying Widow(er) with Dependent Child, check the Head of Household box.' Do not use a QSS->married_filing_jointly mapping for Kansas — compute QSS filers as head_of_household (including the extra HOH exemption). Head of household filers are allowed ONE ADDITIONAL Kansas exemption (K-40 front: 'If filing status above is Head of household, add one exemption'; instructions p. 6: 'If your filing status is Head of Household, you are allowed an additional Kansas exemption'). Include it in exemptions_count or the extra $2,250 allowance will be missed. Disabled Veteran Personal Exemption (new for tax year 2023): an additional $2,250 exemption for an honorably discharged veteran certified by the VA as receiving disability compensation at the 100% rate (permanent, service-sustained). Not auto-applied — include it in exemptions_count only if qualified. If the taxpayer is claimed as a dependent by another taxpayer, the K-40 exemption allowance is $0 (instructions: enter '0' in the Total Kansas exemptions box and on Line 5) — pass exemptions_count = 0. Standard deduction for people 65 or older and/or blind is NOT modeled: the booklet worksheet replaces the base amounts with $4,350/$5,200 (Single, 1/2 boxes), $8,700/$9,400/$10,100/$10,800 (MFJ, 1-4 boxes), $4,700/$5,400/$6,100/$6,800 (MFS, 1-4 boxes), $6,850/$7,700 (HOH, 1/2 boxes) — i.e., +$850 per checked box for Single/HOH and +$700 per box for MFJ/MFS. Compute K-40 Line 4 from that worksheet in those cases. Kansas itemized deductions (Kansas Schedule A, K-40 Line 4) may be claimed instead of the standard deduction even if the federal return did not itemize — itemizers are not modeled; MFS spouses must both itemize if one does. CREDITS are not modeled by this op (they subtract from tax, not from income): the Food Sales Tax Credit is $125 per qualified exemption on K-40 Line 18 (nonrefundable, federal AGI $30,615 or less) — it is a CREDIT, not an income exemption; the Kansas EITC is 17% of the federal EITC (Lines 17/23); credit for child and dependent care expenses is 25% of the federal credit (Line 14); credit for taxes paid to other states (Line 13). Kansas tax on lump sum distributions is not modeled: residents add 13% of the federal Form 4972 tax on K-40 Line 11; Line 12 total income tax = Line 8 + Line 11. Nonresidents and part-year residents are not modeled: they compute the full-year tax on Line 8, then multiply by the Schedule S line B23 nonresident allocation percentage (K-40 Lines 9-10) to get nonresident tax. No mid-year 2023 rate change: the 3.1%/5.25%/5.7% schedule in the final 2023 booklet is the one the 2023 filing season used.
